001: I have to prepare the business trip to Berlin and I don't know where to start.
Don't worry, the first thing is to book the flight and the hotel.
Do you recommend any airline for direct flights?
Yes, there's one that flies direct in the morning and arrives in time for the meeting.
Perfect, then I'll book that one. And do you prefer the hotel near the office?
Of course, that way you'll avoid wasting time commuting during the day.
002: Have you already looked at the itinerary you sent me for the trip?
Yes, I've reviewed it and I think we have very little margin between meetings.
You're right, Tuesday's meeting ends at twelve and the next one starts at twelve thirty.
That's very tight, we'd better move it to the afternoon so we can go at a relaxed pace.
Okay, I'll write to the client to propose the time change.
Good idea, that way we'll also have time to eat without rushing.
003: I don't know what documentation I need for the trip next week.
You need a valid passport and a printed copy of the hotel reservation.
And is the travel insurance covered by the company or do I get it myself?
The company has one, but I recommend you carry the policy with you.
Okay, I'll download it on my phone so I always have it on hand.
Do that, because sometimes they ask for it at customs.
004: How about we prepare tomorrow's presentation for the trade fair together?
Sounds good to me, that way we split the work and we'll be more confident.
I can handle the financial part and you can handle the technical data.
Perfect, I already have some charts prepared from the last meeting.
Great, then we just need to rehearse the presentation once.
Yes, let's meet at five in the conference room and we'll go over the whole thing.
005: Are we bringing promotional materials from the company to the conference?
Yes, I've prepared some new brochures and some business cards.
How many cards do you think we need for the three days?
Two hundred should be enough, but we'd better bring a bit more just in case.
You're right, you never know how many people will come by the booth.
Exactly, and if we see we're running low, we can print more there.
006: Can you help me organize the schedule for the trip to Madrid?
Of course, tell me which meetings you have confirmed and I'll help you arrange them.
I have one on Monday morning and another on Tuesday first thing.
Then I suggest you leave Monday afternoon free for unexpected things.
Good idea, that way I can visit an office if the opportunity comes up.
Sounds like an excellent plan, flexibility always helps in these cases.
007: Have you thought about how we're going to get around the city during the trip?
Yes, I've looked into it and the best option is to take the train, it's fast and punctual.
And what about getting from the hotel to the client's office?
The hotel is a ten-minute walk from the office, you don't need transportation.
That's great, that way we save time and we also stretch our legs.
Definitely, and if it rains, you can always grab a taxi.
008: I'm worried I won't have time to prepare for the meeting with the supplier.
Don't stress, we can go over the key points this very afternoon.
How about we meet after lunch and make an outline?
That sounds perfect, that way we'll arrive at the appointment with clear ideas.
Great, then I'll prepare the documents and let you know when I'm ready.
Okay, in the meantime I'll check the supplier's email.
009: What clothes do you think I should bring on the business trip?
It depends on the weather, but I recommend formal suits and a light coat.
And what about the dinner with the clients on Thursday?
For that occasion, a dark suit is the safest and most elegant option.
You're right, it's better to dress well to make a good impression.
Without a doubt, image also matters in these meetings.
010: Have you confirmed the return time for the trip yet?
Not yet, I was waiting to finalize the last meeting before deciding.
Then I suggest you come back on Friday afternoon, that way you don't have to get up so early.
Yes, and I'll also take advantage of Friday morning to visit the other client.
Sounds like a good strategy, that way you make the most of the trip.
That's the hope, and I'll also avoid the weekend traffic.
